rationale: Two patchable gaps block merge: README documentation is entirely absent (spec required it) and parseAllowList() lacks the spec's two-label minimum enforcement, which lets a single-label entry like '.com' bypass the allow-list for all .com hostnames. A third finding is decision_needed: the Terms & Conditions page renders content fetched at runtime from the backend, so static analysis cannot confirm whether it contains external images — a human must decide whether T&C content is in scope before merge. The decision_needed finding forces confidence: low so the user makes the call rather than any automated resolver.

standards_review.notes: Guide requires EPMCDME-XXXX: Capital sentence (first word must match [A-Z][a-z]*). Branch commits use lowercase first words: 'implement', 'update', 'add'. The CI check runs on the squash merge commit — the squash subject must be 'EPMCDME-12950: Implement image allow-list for LLM markdown output' (capital I) before the MR is merged.
ESLint consistent-return, TypeScript strict errors, and sonarjs/cognitive-complexity violations were all fixed during implementation. No remaining lint blockers.

Core allow-list logic is sound (WHATWG URL parsing, protocol enforcement, XSS-safe HTML escaping). One gap: parseAllowList() accepts single-label entries (e.g. '.com') that would match all hostnames of that TLD via endsWith(). The spec requires a two-label minimum. See CR-002.

findings.title: README not updated; .env missing required inline comment
findings.problem: The spec and plan both required (1) a README subsection documenting VITE_ALLOWED_IMAGE_DOMAINS (format, default, security rationale) and (2) an inline comment on the .env line explaining the comma-separated format. Neither was added. README has zero occurrences of 'VITE_ALLOWED_IMAGE_DOMAINS'.
findings.impact: Operators deploying the feature have no documentation on how to configure the allow-list. The .env line's empty default is unexplained, making it easy to leave blank in production without realising images will be fully blocked.
findings.recommendation: 1) Add a README subsection under the Environment Variables section: 'VITE_ALLOWED_IMAGE_DOMAINS — Comma-separated list of trusted external image domains (e.g. cdn.example.com,.trusted.org). Supports leading-dot wildcard for subdomains. Empty = block all external images (default). Requires two-label minimum per entry.' 2) Add an inline comment on the .env line: '# Comma-separated trusted image domains. Empty = block all external images. Example: cdn.example.com,.trusted.org'

findings.title: parseAllowList() accepts single-label entries — allows entire TLD bypass
findings.problem: parseAllowList() in imageAllowList.ts applies no minimum-label validation. An operator entry like '.com' or 'com' passes through the filter(Boolean) check and reaches matchesAllowListEntry(), where 'evil.com'.endsWith('.com') === true — so every .com hostname is allowed. The spec explicitly requires a two-label minimum (e.g. 'example.com' or '.example.com') to prevent this class of misconfiguration.
findings.impact: A misconfigured allow-list entry (single-label apex like '.com', '.net', '.io') silently grants images from all hostnames under that TLD. This is an exploitable security bypass if an attacker can influence allow-list configuration or if an operator makes a typo.
findings.recommendation: Add label-count enforcement in parseAllowList(): .filter(e => e.replace(/^\./, '').split('.').length >= 2). Also add a test: isImageAllowed('https://evil.com/img.png') with VITE_ALLOWED_IMAGE_DOMAINS='.com' must return false.

findings.title: T&C page content audit not performed — runtime content from backend cannot be statically verified
findings.problem: TermsAndConditionsPage renders content from settings?.content fetched at runtime from the backend API. Static grep cannot confirm the absence of external image URLs in this content. If T&C content ever contains markdown images, those images bypass the allow-list (since the page does not appear to use a patched markdown renderer). The acceptance criterion requires confirmation that T&C content is safe.
findings.impact: If backend-supplied T&C content includes markdown image links to external domains, those images will render without allow-list enforcement — a potential data-exfiltration vector if T&C content is attacker-influenced.
findings.recommendation: Human decision required before merge: (a) Confirm the backend T&C content pipeline never includes external image URLs (backend-side policy / content review), OR (b) Patch TermsAndConditionsPage to use the allow-list-aware markdown renderer for settings?.content rendering. Option (b) is the safer default if T&C content origin cannot be fully controlled.
